<!-- rivetari-judge-review round=1 -->
### Rivetari judge · round 1 · approve

#### Acceptance
- A1: met — cache-usage.test.ts checks that parseClaudeJson returns both cache fields.
- A2: met — tier2-cache-usage.test.ts expects 21_015 tokens, which includes the cache creation and cache read tokens.
- A3: met — estimateCost adds inp*1.25 and inp*0.1 for the cache tokens, and the tests cover both rates.
- A4: met — The new tests cover the no-cache usage, total and cost. Every test file in the diff is new.

<details><summary>2 suggestion(s), non-blocking</summary>

- The cache fields are guarded with `!== undefined`, so null or non-numeric values get through `packages/engine/src/ai/claude-cli.ts:92` — Only spread a cache field when it is a finite number, e.g. `typeof usage.cache_read_input_tokens === "number"`.
- The ai-usage.log record may still leave out the cache tokens `packages/runtime/src/judge/tier2.ts:443` — If the record carries token counts, use the same four-key sum there.

</details>

_Not reviewed: `packages/action/dist/SOURCE_SHA256` (generated), `packages/action/dist/index.js` (generated)._

suggestions.title: The cache fields are guarded with `!== undefined`, so null or non-numeric values get through
suggestions.detail: If the CLI sends `cache_read_input_tokens: null`, the result gains `cacheReadTokens: 0`, so the usage object has a key it didn't have before. A non-numeric string becomes NaN, and NaN poisons tier2's `usage.tokens` and the cost estimate. The existing input and output fields have the same NaN exposure, so this is hardening, not a regression from current CLI output.
suggestions.fix: Only spread a cache field when it is a finite number, e.g. `typeof usage.cache_read_input_tokens === "number"`.

suggestions.title: The ai-usage.log record may still leave out the cache tokens
suggestions.detail: The appendUsage call after this hunk isn't shown. If it records only input and output tokens, the log under-reports the same way the review line did. The card doesn't require a change here, so this doesn't block.
suggestions.repro: Run runTier2 with usageDate set and a cached response, then compare the logged tokens with result.usage.tokens.
suggestions.fix: If the record carries token counts, use the same four-key sum there.
